title: Substitution success probabilities for Theorem-4 cyclic-code authentication
summary: Determine the exact substitution-attack success probabilities for authentication codes based on the remaining dimension-two irreducible cyclic codes.

formal_statement.body: Let $C_N$ be any dimension-two irreducible cyclic code in Theorem 4 of Vega and Hernández, with length $n=q^{N-1}(q-1)/N$ and its source-defined complete weight distribution. For the systematic authentication code constructed from $C_N$, determine the exact maximum substitution-attack success probability $P_S=\max_{u\in\mathbb F_q,\,0\ne c\in C_N}N(u,c)/n$.

scope.domain: Systematic authentication codes constructed from finite-field irreducible cyclic codes
assumptions: C_N is a dimension-two irreducible cyclic code in the source's Theorem 4 family
The authentication code is the source's systematic code based on C_N
P_S is the maximum substitution-attack success probability defined in the source
parameters: the defining irreducible factor and code C_N
scope.unresolved_remainder: The exact P_S value for every Theorem-4 irreducible cyclic code remains unresolved; the source computes only the Theorem-3 family and one example.

citations.label: Vega--Hernández, The Complete Weight Distribution of a Family of Irreducible Cyclic Codes of Dimension Two
citations.locator: Section VII, journal p. 357, paragraph after Theorem 6

progress.summary: The source computes P_S for its Theorem-3 codes and one Theorem-4 example, then explicitly asks for the values for the remaining Theorem-4 family.
citation_labels: Vega--Hernández, The Complete Weight Distribution of a Family of Irreducible Cyclic Codes of Dimension Two
